In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
\ell$-walk MPNNs and second order GNN match the expressive power and computational efficiency of 2 WL and the W[\ell$ walk refinement procedures.
second order graph neural network architectures that allow for non linearity in the layers are not more expressive than their first order counterparts.
the expressive power of \ell$ walk GNNs and second order GNN match 2 WL, and the expressive power of second order G NNs match the expressive power W[\ell$.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
\ell$-walk MPNNs are a new type of graph neural network that match 2WL in expressive power.
the expressive power of GNNs can be improved by increasing the number of layers, by increasing the number (or the depth) of non linear operations per layer and by using more complex features.
the expressive power of GNNs is not improved by allowing more matrix multiplications in layers or by increasing the order of the Weisfeiler Lemann test.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expressive power of graph neural networks is determined by the way in which features are propagated along walks between vertices.

expressive power of GNNs is not affected by the number of layers, the number of dimensions of the features, or the non linearities in layers, but only by the number of walks of length \leq \ell$ that are aggregated in each layer.
, when it comes to distinguishing graphs, there is no need to go beyond the 1 WL test, i.e. there is no benefit in using GNNs with higher dimensional Weisfelier Leman procedures.
